exceptions.reason: The repository intentionally permits authorized maintainers and administrators to facilitate a merge after required checks and review-thread resolution, does not require a code-owner or last-pusher approval, and GitHub cannot count an author's documented maintainer review as a formal approval.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove only after an explicit operator governance decision replaces maintainer/admin facilitation and the replacement remains practical for maintainer-authored changes.

exceptions.target: OpenSSF Scorecard TokenPermissionsID #189 for the npm release version-sync job
exceptions.reason: The protected first-party release job requires contents write access to push its generated version-sync branch and pull-requests write access to open the reviewable sync PR after OIDC publication; every other workflow and job defaults to no token permissions and declares only its own minimum scope.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when version synchronization can use a narrower first-party credential or a separate trusted mechanism without losing protected-environment review, provenance, or atomic release reconciliation.

exceptions.target: OpenSSF Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID #200 and re-fingerprinted duplicate #221 for npm install --package-lock-only
exceptions.reason: The command installs no named or ad hoc package: it deterministically refreshes each committed infrastructure package-lock from that directory's committed package.json after first-party version synchronization, with lifecycle scripts disabled. Scorecard interprets the lockfile operation as an unpinned package invocation even though dependency resolution is committed and subsequently audited.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the release-sync design no longer regenerates infrastructure locks or OpenSSF Scorecard correctly distinguishes lockfile-only refreshes from unpinned package installation.

exceptions.target: TypeScript 6 compatibility API used by ts-jest, ts-node, tsdown, and other compiler-API consumers
exceptions.reason: TypeScript 7.0.2 is the authoritative native CLI compiler but deliberately ships without a stable JavaScript API. The official @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package therefore supplies a peer-compatible API to ts-jest, ts-node, tsdown, and related tools while every direct tsc build and workspace typecheck runs TypeScript 7. This uses the TypeScript team's supported side-by-side layout and no peer override.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove after TypeScript exposes a stable native API, every compiler-API consumer supports it without an override, and the full build, typecheck, declaration, packed-consumer, Jest, conformance, browser/mobile, and infrastructure matrix passes without @typescript/typescript6.

exceptions.target: OpenSSF Scorecard BinaryArtifactsID #196 and #197 for @bsv/verifast WASM
exceptions.reason: The two checked-in WASM modules are required runtime artifacts for browser, worker, ESM, CommonJS, and classic-script consumers. Their pinned BDK source, reproducible build, SHA-256 values, generated-file ownership, ABI tests, package-consumer tests, and bundle budget are enforced; removing them would break zero-install and browser package consumers.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove only when all supported package consumers can obtain the verified WASM reproducibly without install-time network access, lifecycle scripts, mutable build inputs, or a larger supply-chain risk.

exceptions.reason: Jest 30.4.2 still constrains its reporting and coverage paths to minimatch releases that require brace-expansion 1.x/2.x, while GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg is fixed only in brace-expansion 5.0.8.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove after the supported Jest dependency graph adopts minimatch 10.2.5 or newer and natively resolves brace-expansion 5.0.8 or newer.

exceptions.reason: Stryker 9.6.1 is current but its current typed-rest-client 2.3.1 dependency pins vulnerable qs 6.15.1 exactly. GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26 is fixed in qs 6.15.2 and later, so a parent-scoped substitution to 6.15.3 is the narrowest durable remediation. The previous lock-only selection was lost when an unrelated dependency change regenerated the graph.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when Stryker no longer depends on typed-rest-client 2.3.1 or a supported typed-rest-client release natively depends on qs 6.15.2 or newer, then regenerate the lock and rerun the complete mutation campaign.

exceptions.reason: The latest openapi-typescript release still depends on Redocly 1.x ranges that resolve vulnerable js-yaml and minimatch paths, so the isolated codegen lock substitutes compatible patched releases and verifies the generated output byte-for-byte.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when a supported openapi-typescript release natively resolves non-vulnerable js-yaml, minimatch, and brace-expansion versions, then regenerate and compare every committed output.

exceptions.target: 211 individually reasoned conformance cases across 19 governed vector files
exceptions.reason: Every current non-run vector has a stable ID and inherited or local reason, and every affected file has an exact count, classification, owner, review date, and removal condition. The remaining gaps require stateful/funded/overlay fixtures, upstream parity decisions, or runner work before enforcement can require zero skips.
exceptions.removeWhen: Every conformance skip is implemented or documented as deliberately unsupported with a permanent compatibility decision.

exceptions.target: 6 governed direct skips in required package tests
exceptions.reason: Manual, live, and resource suites are now classified outside deterministic PR discovery. Six required-suite gaps remain individually registered with owner, reason, review date, and removal condition; CI rejects new anonymous skips, stale registrations, and empty test bodies.
exceptions.removeWhen: All six required-suite gaps are enabled, moved to a correctly governed non-PR suite, or removed with evidence that the scenario is obsolete.

exceptions.target: sonar-project.properties and .sonarcloud.properties broad test and generated-file exclusions
exceptions.reason: Legacy Sonar configuration excludes tests broadly and suppresses duplication findings while generated and third-party artifacts are mixed into repository paths; project administration cannot be changed during the current wave.
exceptions.removeWhen: The Sonar backlog wave proves precise source, test, generated, vendored, and coverage boundaries and removes broad exclusions without hiding real findings.

exceptions.target: typescript:S6564 on documented primitive aliases in SDK Wallet.interfaces.ts, remittance/types.ts, and wallet/validationHelpers.ts
exceptions.reason: These aliases are the named BRC-100 and remittance wire vocabulary. Their exported names and JSDoc constraints carry defaults, units, ranges, encodings, and generated-documentation anchors that a bare boolean, number, or string cannot express. Removing them would degrade a stable public declaration and documentation contract without changing runtime or TypeScript assignability.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the analyzer distinguishes documented public protocol aliases, or when an SDK major version can adopt a compatibility-preserving nominal representation with generated documentation and packed-consumer proof.
